subject: Detecting Gerygone in the secondary forest

messages.author: 90e03903624b92b5
messages.subject: Detecting Gerygone in the secondary forest
parts:
Hello everyone,
First off, thanks for the great R package!

I have done some test recordings with Song Meters in secondary forest in Sumatra. Now I am comparing the performance and usefulness of Song Scope to Seewave for our research. I have been working on it for a while, but I stumble upon a problem:

I want to compare a reference call of 3 seconds to a 100s recording which I know contains 5 other calls of the bird Gerygone sulphurea.

I kept only frequencies between 3500 and 5000 Hz. I use covspectro (corenv never ended) to compare the reference call:

to successive parts of the 100s recording, extracted with cutw. The problem is, the extracted parts look like that:

although in the original spectogram, the parts are white and relatively silent, only containing background noise. I guess the spectrograms use red for the highest amplitude (even if it is low) and color the other sounds relative to the loudest sound.
However, the correlations between my reference call and those background noise parts are highly significant (coef>90%) and the time offset is always 0. There is no way to distinguish really significant correlations (between two real calls) from unsignificant ones (between reference call and background noise). Is there a way to disable the amplitude autoscaling such that comparisons with background noise do not turn out so significant?
I attach my code here:
rm(list = ls())
setwd("D:/Burung")
library(seewave)
library(tuneR)
freq=22050
song<-readWave("original_part.wav")

songf<-resamp(song,f=44100,g=freq,output="Wave")
songf<-ffilter(songf,from=3500,to=5000,output="Wave")

reff<-cutw(songf,from=10.75,to=13.75,plot=FALSE,output="Wave")

RESU=NULL
dura=trunc(length(songf)/freq)
refd=trunc(length(reff)/freq)
bins<-seq(from=1,to=trunc(dura),by=refd/2)
pb <- txtProgressBar(min=0,max=max(bins),style=3)

for (i in bins){
  scan<-cutw(songf,from=i,to=i+refd,output="Wave")
  resu<-covspectro(reff,scan,f=freq,n=15,plot=FALSE)
  RESU<-cbind(RESU,resu)
  Sys.sleep(0.1)
  setTxtProgressBar(pb,i)
}
close(pb)
Am I doing a mistake?
I would like to add that it would be handy if covspectro could compare time waves of different lengths.
Greetings from Sumatra

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Detecting Gerygone in the secondary forest
parts:
Hi Kevin,

Your issue seems to be due to the normalisation applied by spectro()
on the spectroram matrix as discussed by Mike Crowe. An option will be
available in the next release of seewave to turn off this normalisation.

To be honest, I am not sure seewave will be the best tool for
automatic ID. I guess Songscope will do it better and, above all, much
faster.

Thanks for using seewave,

Best

Jerome
